From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Zhao <alex.zhao@lumosai.com>
Cc: Bethany Ruiz <bethany.ruiz@lumosai.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 13:02:00 -0800
Subject: Integration sizing & continuous-batch assumptions — follow-up and next steps

Alex / Bethany — thanks again for the call earlier today. Short recap and a few asks so we can produce an accurate unit-econ/ops recommendation: 

Recap from our end:
- Target integration: LumosAI inference endpoint (customer-facing product) that will call Redwood for text generation & light reranking.
- Expected steady-state: ~120M tokens/day during daytime window; expected peak bursts up to 7x for short periods (black Friday-like traffic but on a smaller scale).
- Primary KPIs you care about: latency p95 < 300ms for single-turn interactions, predictable monthly spend (budget range), and a target billable of ~$800–1,200 per 1M tokens (open to adjustment based on SLA/features).
- Workload pattern: high number of short prompts (~20–60 prompt+completion tokens median), plus a subset of longer completions for document summarization (~800 tokens). Streaming will be used for long completions.

Specific asks (so we can return a crisp recommendation + pricing):
1) Please confirm the steady-state and peak token/day numbers (you can provide ranges if uncertain).
2) Confirm whether streaming completions should be treated differently for billing target (i.e., do you have separate $/1M target for streaming flows?).
3) Any constraints on concurrency (max concurrent users/streams) or SLOs we should assume besides the p95 above?

What we’ll provide after we get the confirmations:
- A short calc (attached) showing estimated unit cost at 1M / 10M / 100M token scales for 3 batching/concurrency configurations (aggressive batching, balanced continuous-batching, low-latency shallow-batching).
- Recommended serving config (batch window, concurrency target, caching hints, KV cache expectations) and expected effective batching utilization.

I’ve attached the preliminary unit-econ workbook we used in the call. If you can reply with the three confirmations above, we’ll turn around the config + pricing math by EOD Tuesday.

Best,
Marissa

marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0132

Thanks Marissa — good summary. Quick clarifications below: 

1) Tokens/day: the 120M is our current internal estimate for the core product (US/EMEA users). We expect a conservative growth range of 80–150M/day over the next 6–9 months; can you model both 100M and 150M/day?

2) Streaming: for the long-run we treat streaming and non-streaming tokens equivalently from a business-target perspective — so the $/1M target is the same. Operationally, we understand streaming has different latency characteristics; we mainly want budget predictability.

3) Concurrency/SLOs: Our product team expects to have ~1.2k concurrent interactive users at peak; average session concurrency per user is low (~1.0–1.3). For backend burst tolerance, we'd like config that supports 2k short-lived concurrent streams without large latency degradation.

Budget target: we are aiming for a price closer to $850/1M tokens as the preferred target for a committed/volume-discount tier. If there are features (long-term caching, prefix caching) that materially move the number, call them out.

If you can show the 100M and 150M/day scenarios and a sensitivity to batching (effective batch util 60% / 80% / 95%) that would be perfect. Looking forward to the calc.

—Alex

Marissa / Rishi — here's a concise ops + unit-econ sketch based on the confirmed numbers. I kept the assumptions explicit so we can push back on the Lumos team items if needed.

Assumptions (please validate with Alex):\- Token mix (short interactive flows): median prompt 25 tokens, median completion 55 tokens -> prompt:completion token split ≈ 31:69 by tokens.
- Long-document summarization: typical prompt ~1,200 tokens, completion ~800 tokens (these are ~5% of total volume).
- Effective model: 7B-class open model with quantization; baseline throughput measured on our infra: 80 tokens/s per stream at 16-bit-ish path, batching optimizations increase aggregate throughput per GPU.
- KV cache applicable for repeated user context prefixes — conservative hit: 15% overall for interactive flows; optimistic 35% for sessions that reuse history.

Batching / concurrency guidance:\- Continuous-batching window: 120–200 ms as a default for interactive flows to balance latency and utilization. For more aggressive throughput focus we can push to 300–350 ms, but p95 latency will move up.
- Expected effective batch utilization: 60% (low), 80% (balanced), 95% (aggressive) — these map to average effective tokens-per-batch of ~1.2k / 1.7k / 2.1k respectively given Lumos token mix.
- Concurrency assumptions: baseline 1.2k concurrent streams -> translate to ~24 active generation workers per GPU shard in our tests with balanced batching; high-burst 2k concurrent -> requires either additional reserved shards or lower batch windows to avoid queueing.

Unit-econ (headline estimates; exact workbook attached):\- Scenario A: 100M tokens/day
  - 60% util -> estimated infra-backed cost -> $1,100 / 1M tokens (no committed discount)
  - 80% util -> estimated -> $920 / 1M tokens
  - 95% util -> estimated -> $760 / 1M tokens
\- Scenario B: 150M tokens/day
  - 60% util -> $980 / 1M tokens
  - 80% util -> $820 / 1M tokens
  - 95% util -> $680 / 1M tokens

Notes / tradeoffs:
- These numbers assume: our balanced quantized kernel paths, average sequence lengths above, and no long-tailed classification workloads that occupy GPU for long (we should identify any such flows).
- Streaming long completions count towards tokens; operationally you pay per token the same, but concurrency/latency behavior differs — streaming requests tie up streams longer, which reduces effective batch opportunities for other short requests. That’s reflected in the util numbers above.
- If Lumos can commit to a 6–12 month committed usage tier we can take another ~12–18% off the listed $/1M via reserved capacity pricing.

Next steps:
1) Marissa — send these headline numbers to Alex (I can sync if they want a short call).
2) Rishi — can you produce a 1-slide ops summary (batch window, throttle guidance, fallback model variant) and an updated workbook with the exact per-GPU shard math for the 100M/150M cases?
3) Marissa / Lumos — confirm whether they want a committed-tier proposal or a sample POC month to validate effective batch util.

I can iterate quickly if Alex pushes new token assumptions.

—Laura
